name: Artlist
editorial: For Artlist, separate your needs for music, effects, footage, and AI assets before comparing plans. Choose one real project and note how many assets of each kind reach the final edit; browsing volume is not a cost measure. Read current license coverage for client delivery, ads, and distribution channels rather than relying on a generic label. Store the asset URL and license record with the project so the team can answer a later rights question. Test a replacement asset to see whether search and download fit your deadline. Artlist is worth evaluating when your work centers on creative asset licensing. Start with a documentary teaser and a sponsored social cut; these two deliverables expose different constraints, so a single polished demo is a poor buying test. For the first, write down the time spent preparing source material, making the initial cut, and correcting mistakes. For the second, repeat the process with a fresh asset rather than reusing a finished template. This gives you a practical comparison of effort across routine and less predictable work. Pay particular attention to music searches, footage needs, and license records. Ask a colleague to open the exported result on another device and note any missing captions, clipped audio, font substitution, or awkward pacing. Keep the source file so you can measure how painful a late revision would be. A workflow that feels fast for one person may slow down when another person has to review it. Before paying, check which subscription covers the intended distribution and asset types. Read the current checkout and license terms directly on the merchant site, since plan names and entitlements can change. Save a dated screenshot of the offer and renewal conditions, then compare the total cost over the period you will actually use the tool. If you are buying for a team, assign one person to test access, permissions, and export ownership. This evaluation is our editorial method, not a claim that a discount is available today.
refund_policy: Check current merchant terms; not independently verified.
